records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController update/destroy raise NoMethodError (500) instead of 404 when the id is stale/unknown because the nil record isn't handled
records.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy, the record is fetched with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If the id is stale/unknown, `host` will be nil. `update` then calls `save_host(host)` which immediately does `host.host = ...` causing NoMethodError, and `destroy` calls `host.destroy` causing NoMethodError. There is no 404/handled error path in the diff.

records.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch (`if (m[2])`) assumes `obj[k]` is an array and immediately does `obj[k].map(...)`. If a server payload includes `*_ids: null` (or any non-array), this will throw a `TypeError`. The diff adds this plural hydration logic but does not add a null/array guard, so the defect is introduced/exposed by this change.

records.issue_text: Frontend destroyRecord() has no .catch, so delete failures are silent and the row stays in the table with no error shown
records.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` but does not attach a `.catch(...)`. If the DELETE request fails/rejects, no error is shown (unlike `save()` which uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)`), and the `deleteHost` action is never sent, so the row will remain with a silent failure.
